name: Parliament Hill
description: Also known as Kite Hill. Its protected view takes in the City, St Paul's Cathedral and Canary Wharf.

name: Hampstead Heath summit
description: The highest ground on the Heath, by Whitestone Pond and Jack Straw's Castle.

name: Preacher's Hill
description: Rise on the East Heath above the Hampstead Ponds.

name: Boudicca's Mound
description: Bronze Age bell barrow (tumulus), linked by legend with Queen Boudicca's grave.

name: Sandy Heath
description: Wooded area west of Spaniards Road, marked by Victorian sand quarrying.

name: Vale of Health
description: Small hamlet in a hollow, surrounded on every side by the Heath.

name: Hampstead Heath Extension
description: Former farmland added to the Heath in 1907, with open playing fields and hedgerows.

name: Kenwood House
description: Neoclassical villa by Robert Adam with a fine art collection (Rembrandt, Vermeer). Free entry.

name: Hill Garden and Pergola
description: Edwardian raised pergola walkway and gardens, built for Lord Leverhulme.

name: Golders Hill Park Zoo
description: Small free zoo with deer, donkeys, lemurs and birds.

name: Stone of Free Speech
description: Stone where public speakers are said to have gathered since the 19th century.

name: Whitestone Pond
description: Pond at the top of Hampstead, next to the Heath's highest point.

name: The Spaniards Inn
description: 16th-century inn linked with Dick Turpin, Keats and Dickens.

name: Jack Straw's Castle
description: Former coaching inn named after a leader of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt.

name: Parliament Hill Lido
description: Unheated 1938 stainless-steel lido, open all year round.

name: Mixed Bathing Pond
description: Open-water swimming pond on the Hampstead side.

name: Men's Bathing Pond
description: Open-water swimming pond on the Highgate side.

name: Kenwood Ladies' Bathing Pond
description: Secluded open-water swimming pond near Kenwood.

name: Parliament Hill Athletics Track
description: Public 400m track, home to the Highgate Harriers.

name: Keats House
description: Regency house where John Keats wrote 'Ode to a Nightingale'.

name: Burgh House
description: Queen Anne house from 1704, now the Hampstead Museum.

name: Fenton House
description: 17th-century merchant's house with a walled garden and an early keyboard collection (National Trust).

name: 2 Willow Road
description: Ernő Goldfinger's modernist home from 1939 (National Trust).

name: Highgate Cemetery
description: Victorian cemetery with Egyptian Avenue and the grave of Karl Marx.

name: Lauderdale House
description: Tudor house in Waterlow Park, now an arts centre and café.
